## TL;DR

Addressed review finding #1 by adding fixture-driven task create/edit interaction coverage across the phone, tablet and desktop widths. The first implementation only extended a static picker overflow test; the reviewer correctly found that it did not verify task creation, editing, field saves or screenshot handling. The expanded tests pass locally at 375, 768 and 1280 px.

## Work and rationale

I re-read the current review report and followed its named bug class through the responsive picker test, drawer field tests and QA document. The blocker was incomplete responsive QA evidence, not a discovered product defect. I added `task-create-edit-responsive.test.ts`, which mounts the real task drawer with repository fixtures and stubs persistence so assertions cover the data sent on create and save. It checks empty-title validation, manual create, priority and area model updates, dependency data, queued screenshot upload and details editing at each target width.

The test also mounts the actual dependency picker with candidate-task fixtures at each width and clicks its candidate and removal controls. The existing headless WebKit test checks real rendered picker overflow at 375, 768 and 1280 px. This separates responsive drawer interaction coverage from browser geometry coverage and keeps both forms of evidence concrete.

I rewrote the QA document to describe precisely what the tests prove. It now identifies component-level viewport coverage, the WebKit overflow check, mocked repository writes and screenshot upload limitations. It does not characterize a queued image fixture as a live external upload.

## Approaches tried

I initially attempted to drive the task drawer’s custom teleported controls through selectors in the component test. The test environment’s portal and Radix behavior did not expose those popover options consistently, even though the rendered form controls and save wiring were present. I changed the fixture suite to drive the child component model events for area and priority and verified the resulting create/patch payloads. Dependency selection/removal remains a direct click against the actual picker component’s rendered fixture options. The screenshot fixture is queued in the UI store and the upload call is asserted against the created ID.

I ran the new test file directly while iterating. The repository test wrapper combines its configured retry count with a passed `--retry=0`, producing a CLI argument error after the test run; I removed that override. The test assertions themselves passed in the successful targeted execution.

## Challenges and blockers

TaskDrawer mounts with asynchronous repository initialization, and several controls use teleported popovers. The fixture setup waits for initialization and uses stable component-level interactions where the test DOM cannot reliably operate Radix portal content. No external dependencies, configuration changes or app layout changes were required. This pass does not claim complete physical-device layout inspection or a real screenshot upload service outcome.

## Key learnings

Responsive test claims need to identify whether they come from a layout-capable browser or a component test with a viewport value. The standalone browser test gives real geometry evidence for the dependency picker; the drawer interaction matrix confirms the form-to-store create and edit payloads at the specified width settings. Keeping those scopes explicit makes the report auditable and avoids overstating what the fixtures prove.
